catalog_quote: [StressTyp2 passage 1975, Reesink 1987:39] Stress in usan cannot be predicted. Each grammatical word may receive primary stress. Polysyllabic words in context cannot obscure their inherent stress. Monosyllabic words have their stress reduced considerably when the primary stress of a stress group is assigned somewhere else. Stress also plays a role in the morphology. ... [Pick 2020:31-32] On the other hand, Reesink (1987: 39-40) characterizes stress in Usan as phonemic, and illustrates this with minimal pairs that differ only in stress, such as [go.ˈbi] 'a tree', and [ˈgo.bi] 'taro seedling'. ... [fn.11] Reesink does not make clear whether in Usan stress placement generally follows certain patterns, but has exceptions, as in Pamosu, or whether it is completely unpredictable. ... [Pick 2020 ch.10] Stress, which is phonemic in Usan, may play a role, and this possibility warrants further investiga…

audit.reasoning: The classification (lexical/unpredictable stress, no weight conditioning, no secondary stress described) rests on the phonology chapter of the only reference grammar of Usan (Reesink 1987:39-40), which is the best available description; no later phonology or instrumental study exists in Glottolog or could be found. The quotation is verified verbatim in the held StressTyp2 database (passage 1975, p.39) and independently corroborated by Pick 2020 (held PDF, pp.31-32, fn.11, ch.10) with stress-only minimal pairs, and by WALS's independent reading of Reesink 1987 (No fixed stress / Lexical). Nothing suggests the coding is wrong; the record's own correction of Gordon 2002 and StressTyp2-SPD 'penult' is sound (goˈbi vs ˈgobi falsifies fixed penult at length 2). It is not 'well-sourced' only because pp.39-40 of the primary are not held and were read through carriers; obtaining Reesink 1987 ch.2
